description: A column DEFAULT that is a non-literal EXPRESSION (arithmetic, concatenation, function call, CASE) is evaluated per row at INSERT time, instead of the raw expression text being stored as the value - DEFAULT 10 + 5 yields 15, not the string '10 + 5'. Literal defaults are unchanged, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP still resolves to a real value, a default naming a bare identifier is refused at CREATE with 'invalid identifier' (the table never exists), and an explicit value overrides an expression default. Converted 1:1 from features/DefaultExpressionEvaluationTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, qty INTEGER DEFAULT 10 + 5)
INSERT INTO t (id) VALUES (1)
SELECT qty FROM t WHERE id = 1
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR DEFAULT 'Mr. ' || 'Unknown')
INSERT INTO t (id) VALUES (1)
SELECT name FROM t WHERE id = 1
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, upper_name VARCHAR DEFAULT UPPER('test'))
INSERT INTO t (id) VALUES (1)
SELECT upper_name FROM t WHERE id = 1
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, priority VARCHAR DEFAULT CASE WHEN 1 = 1 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END)
INSERT INTO t (id) VALUES (1)
SELECT priority FROM t WHERE id = 1
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, status VARCHAR DEFAULT 'active')
INSERT INTO t (id) VALUES (1)
SELECT status FROM t WHERE id = 1
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, n INTEGER DEFAULT 42)
INSERT INTO t (id) VALUES (1)
SELECT n FROM t WHERE id = 1
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
INSERT INTO t (id) VALUES (1)
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM t WHERE id = 1 AND created_at IS NOT NULL
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, x VARCHAR DEFAULT (badcol))
SHOW TABLES LIKE 't'

INSERT INTO t (id, qty) VALUES (1, 99)
